content.text: In regions where [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-explained-digital-creators-7|COREMERCH guide to payment]]-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-first-principles-definitive-3|Payment Options]]-methods-filipino-digital-creators-which-architecture-actually-2|payment]] processors like Stripe and PayPal are not an option, digital creators face significant barriers when trying to sell their products. Countries such as Nigeria and Venezuela are examples where creators are locked out of conventional payment solutions. This guide will show you how to deploy a digital store using Supabase as your order database without relying on these restricted platforms.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Stack 01 — the Sovereign Starter Stack — uses GitHub Pages for storefront hosting, Google Apps Script as the backend Web App, Google Sheets as the order database, Google Drive for product file storage, and Gmail for delivery email. The entire stack costs nothing per month. Google Apps Script runs in response to webhook events from NOWPayments, validates the payment, logs the order to Google Sheets, generates a receipt, and sends a Gmail delivery email with a Google Drive shared link. The daily limits on the free tier are adequate for most creators at the early and growth stages.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Stack 02 — the Edge Commerce Stack — uses Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling, Supabase for order storage, Cloudflare R2 for product file delivery, and Resend for transactional email. The entire stack costs nothing per month up to significant volume thresholds — Cloudflare Workers provides 100,000 requests per day free, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage free, Cloudflare R2 provides 10GB storage and zero egress fees free, and Resend provides 3,000 emails per month free. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are configured during COREMERCH deployment.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

The NOWPayments configuration sequence is the same regardless of which stack you are deploying. Create a NOWPayments account — no KYC required, no document upload, no bank account needed. Navigate to the wallet settings and add the wallet addresses for each cryptocurrency you want to accept. USDT on Tron and Bitcoin are the practical starting point for most creators in restricted markets. Generate an API key from the NOWPayments dashboard. Set the webhook endpoint URL in the NOWPayments IPN settings pointing to your Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App. Set the webhook secret key — a string you generate that both NOWPayments and your backend know.
You control your data and transactions without reliance on external platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Configure your digital store to accept over 300 cryptocurrencies effortlessly.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

The setup decision comes down to time versus depth. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything to build Stack 01 yourself in an afternoon or Stack 02 over a weekend — full source code, step-by-step configuration, and the NOWPayments integration guide. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH build Stack 02 for you in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured for email deliverability. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. Both are at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?
Use GitHub Pages for hosting and Supabase for managing orders. Integrate NOWPayments to handle cryptocurrency transactions without fees. This keeps your operations secure and under your control.
What is the difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 in COREMERCH?

Stack 01 utilizes GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, while Stack 02 employs Cloudflare Pages and Workers with Supabase. Stack 02 offers enhanced capabilities and is deployed in 48 hours, fully tested before handoff.
Can I host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages?
Yes, both platforms allow you to host a digital product store. GitHub Pages is ideal for simple setups, while Cloudflare Pages offers greater scalability and speed for larger operations.
What tools do I need to set up my digital store?
You will need GitHub for hosting, Supabase for your order database, and NOWPayments for handling crypto transactions. Additional tools for file delivery include Google Drive or Cloudflare R2.
How long does it take to deploy Stack 01?
Deploying Stack 01 typically takes 4-6 hours following the Sovereign Blueprint. This allows for a quick setup to get your digital store operational.
